newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-JANCKER SAVES THE DAY FOR BAYERN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-JANCKER SAVES THE DAY FOR BAYERN.

text.p: A late goal by Carsten Jancker earned nine-man Bayern Munich a 3-3 draw against local rivals 1860 Munich in a pulsating derby in the Olympic Stadium on Sunday.
Two goals by Horst Heldt gave 1860 an early lead before Bayern hit back through German internationals Juergen Klinsmann and Mehmet Scholl.
1860 looked to have their first win over their arch rivals since 1977 in the bag when substitute Joerg Boehme made it 3-2 with his first kick in the 82nd minute.

But Bayern, down to nine men after wing back Christian Ziege and captain Lothar Matthaeus were dismissed for second bookable offences, salvaged a point thanks to a spectacular strike from Jancker just two minutes from time.

A win would have put Bayern five points clear of second-placed Bayer Leverkusen, who drew 2-2 with Borussia Moenchengladbach on Saturday. But coach Giovanni Trapattoni had nothing but praise for his players.
"I'm very very satisfied because derbies are always dangerous," the former Juventus, Internazionale and AC Milan boss said. "We're still three points ahead of Leverkusen."
The 185th meeting between the two Munich sides produced several candidates for Germany's goal of the season.
Heldt set the standard in the 15th minute, running almost the entire length of the field before expertly slotting the ball past Oliver Kahn from the edge of the box.
He added a second just three minutes later after Olaf Bodden was brought down in the box. Kahn parried Heldt's penalty but the former Cologne player followed up to ram the ball home.
Klinsmann scored with a bullet header, his 13th Bundesliga goal of the season, just before halftime to give Bayern some hope as they went into the break.
Scholl, who replaced Dietmar Hamann during the interval, brought Bayern level in the 59th minute, dribbling past several 1860 defenders on the edge of the box before firing the ball home.
Despite Ziege's dismissal midway through the second half, Bayern looked set to hold on at 2-2 until 1860 coach Werner Lorant brought on Joerg Boehme in the 82nd minute.

The 23-year-old midfielder cut back inside the Bayern area with his first touch and then rifled a vicious shot past Kahn. Bayern's misery was compounded moments later when Matthaeus received his marching orders.
But it was another substitute who had the final say. Jancker, who replaced Klinsmann in the 70th minute, turned brilliantly inside the area and shot past Rainer Berg in the 1860 goal.
Lorant was disappointed not to have claimed all three points but concentrated on the positive aspects of the game.
"This was a very good Bundesliga game -- the spectators saw six goals and I think everyone would go home happy," he said.
Asked if Swiss defender Marco Walker would get a lashing from the coach's notoriously sharp tongue for allowing Jancker to turn inside the box, Lorant replied: "We'll deal with that internally."
Teams:

1860 - 12-Rainer Berg; 6-Bernhard Trares; 4-Marco Walker, 7-Horst Heldt (19-Abedi Pele 65), 15-Holger Greilich, 22-Matthias Hamann; 10-Peter Nowak, 20-Miroslav Stevic, 33-Manfred Bender; 13-Harald Cerny, 9-Olaf Bodden.

Bayern - 1-Oliver Kahn; 10-Lothar Matthaeus; 2-Markus Babbel, 5-Thomas Helmer, 17-Christian Ziege, 16-Dietmar Hamann (7-Mehmet Scholl 46); 6-Christian Nerlinger, 8-Thomas Strunz, 21-Alexander Zickler; 20-Ruggiero Rizzitelli (3-Markus Muench 74), 18-Juergen Klinsmann (19-Carsten Jancker 70).
